title: Neonatal jaundice
presentation: A baby admitted with jaundice. Consultant asked: why might a baby be admitted with jaundice, and what is the systematic way to think about causes?

pathway.title: Bilirubin pathway
pathway.mermaid:
flowchart LR
 A[Red cell breakdown] --> B[Haem to biliverdin to unconjugated bilirubin]
 B --> C[Bound to albumin in blood]
 C --> D[Hepatocyte uptake]
 D --> E[Conjugation by UGT1A1]
 E --> F[Conjugated bilirubin into bile]
 F --> G[Gut: urobilinogen and stercobilin]
 G --> H[Stool colour]
 G --> I[Reabsorbed: enterohepatic circulation]
 I --> J[Urine urobilinogen]
 I --> D

management: Plot bilirubin on the NICE treatment threshold chart for gestational age and age in hours.
Phototherapy converts unconjugated bilirubin to water-soluble isomers.
Exchange transfusion for severe hyperbilirubinaemia or rapid rise (specialist decision).
Refer urgently if conjugated jaundice is found.
redFlags: Lethargy, poor feeding, high-pitched cry or arching (possible bilirubin encephalopathy)
pearls: Think pathway: where in the pathway is the block, before, in, or after the liver?
Conjugated jaundice is never normal in a newborn.
Check the stool colour. It is quick and tells you about bile flow.

selfTest.q: Name the three levels used to classify the causes of jaundice.
Why are the stools pale and urine dark in obstructive jaundice?
selfTest.a: Conjugated bilirubin cannot reach the gut, so no stercobilin forms; conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble and spills into urine.

selfTest.q: What does jaundice in the first 24 hours suggest?
selfTest.a: Pathological cause, typically haemolysis or infection.
